plate_findings.evidence: Alopecia over scalp, eyebrows, lower eyelid sparing upper eyelid
Involvement of trunk in the form of ichthyosis with erythema and brownish adherent scaling

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 5 panels (A, B, C, D, E). A: Infant face showing alopecia of scalp, eyebrows and lower eyelid, a classic cutaneous feature of KID syndrome in an article titled on an infant with KID syndrome. B: Trunk ichthyosis with erythema and brownish adherent scaling, consistent with the ichthyotic erythrokeratoderma plaques of KID syndrome. C: Perianal hyperkeratotic brownish plaque, a hyperkeratotic plaque manifestation of KID syndrome ichthyosis. D: Stippled keratoderma of the sole is the characteristic palmoplantar keratoderma of KID syndrome. E: Symmetrical erythematous macerated plaques of both groins in the same KID syndrome infant; flexural involvement is a recognized but less highlighted manifestation, so the finding is recorded as a proposed term.

plate_findings.evidence: Rippled hyperkeratotic plaques on the knees
Hypotrichosis of the eyelashes and eyebrows; aged facial appearance

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F). A: Case 1 clinical photo of plantar keratoderma, a classic KID syndrome manifestation; article title confirms KID syndrome. B: Case 1 rippled hyperkeratotic plaques on knees, characteristic KID syndrome skin finding. C: Case 1 facial photo showing sparse eyebrows/eyelashes and thickened facial skin, typical of KID syndrome. D: Case 1 eye photo showing vascularizing keratitis, a defining feature of KID syndrome (the keratitis component). E: Case 2 palmar hyperkeratosis, classic KID syndrome palmoplantar keratoderma. F: Case 2 scalp showing alopecia with ichthyosiform erythrokeratoderma, characteristic KID syndrome.
panels.attribution_text: Wonkam et al. Heterozygous p.Asp50Asn mutation in the GJB2 gene in two Cameroonian patients with keratitis-ichthyosis-deafness (KID) syndrome.. BMC medical genetics 2013. doi:10.1186/1471-2350-14-81. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Illustrations of some clinical features of the two Cameroonian KID cases (Case 1; panels A-D; Case 2 panels E and F). A) Keratoderma of the soles B) Rippled hyperkeratotic plaques on the knees; C) Hypotrichosis of the eyelashes and eyebrows; D) Mild vascularizing keratitis; E) Hyperkeratosis of the hands; F) Alopecia, hypotrichosis, ichthyosiform erythrokeratoderma.
in_text_mentions: development was normal; however, physical examination revealed a generalized thickened skin and xeroderma, palmoplantar keratoderma and rippled hyperkeratotic plaques on the knees and elbows (Figure 1A-D). She had aged facial appearance, hypotrichosis (sparse of eyelashes and eyebrows), and hyperkeratosis lesions in the external auditory canal. Ophthalmologic examination revealed a mild vascularizing keratitis which explained her photophobia and reduced visual acuity. Oral examination showed dental dysplasia and histopathological examination of the skin revealed an acanthotic dyskeratosis. Th

e health facility physical examination revealed generalized ichthyosiform erythrokeratoderma, palmoplantar keratoderma, alopecia universalis and atrichosis (absence of eyelashes and eyebrows) (Figure 1E-F). Joint mobility of the elbows, knees and ankles was seriously reduced by keratoderma. She had photophobia and ocular irritation, and an ophthalmologic examination revealed a vascularizing keratitis.
